rule: Defer reply body literal couples to deferred-marker classifier regex
description: P3 coupling. The defer reply body EMITTED by `plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/reply-resolve.sh` and the deferred-marker regex READ by `plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/fix-history-classify.jq` are a producer/consumer pair across two files: the classifier recognises a thread as already-deferred ONLY by matching the exact byte sequence the emitter writes, so a one-sided edit silently re-raises every deferred thread as unhandled and drives duplicate defer replies. Three spans carry that coupling and each fails independently. The SOURCE pin is the emitter's body assignment — the `Deferred to ` prefix and the period that terminates the tracked home are exactly what the regex anchors on. The FIRST consumer pin is the classifier's executable `test("Deferred to [^[:space:]]+\\.")` call, pinned inside its enclosing `select(...)` so the pin cannot drift onto the sibling `Fixed in` marker test. The SECOND consumer pin sits back in the emitter on the `invalid-tracked-home` guard, because `[^[:space:]]+` only matches BY CONSTRUCTION while a whitespace-bearing (or flag-shaped) tracked home is rejected before the body is ever built; deleting that guard breaks the coupling while both marker spans stay intact, which is why it is pinned separately rather than folded into the source span. What this fixture honestly guarantees is exactly that these three word sequences exist in these two named files. It does NOT assert that the regex MATCHES the body: a presence pin executes neither side. Behavioural proof of the match lives in `tools/test_reply_resolve.sh` and `tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh`, over the deferred-marker case fixture under `tests/fix-history/`. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a coordinated rewrite that changes BOTH literals consistently is invisible, and legitimately so — this pin protects the pair from ONE-SIDED drift, never from a joint redefinition; (2) a rewrite-around is outside its reach — a second emission site writing a different body, or a second classifier arm reading a different marker, is in neither pinned span, and a NEW reader that never carries the marker at all is an absence defect no fixture in this directory can detect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract; (3) the pin claims nothing about the sibling `Fixed in <SHA>.` marker, nor about which disposition the agent chose; the sanctioned-route coupling that decides when the defer body is emitted at all is guarded by `tests/policy/safety-defer-with-scope-reply-route.json`.
